tour.locked: Sign in to open this one — it reads your own data.
tour.launch_caption: Walks through every feature and where it lives, and tells you what changed in the latest release.
tour.finished: Tour finished — reopen it any time from Profile.
tour.news_intro: Shipped since you were last here.
tour.welcome_body: TopStocks turns a broker statement into your real numbers: FIFO lots, P/L in your own currency at the ECB rate of each trade's own date, and what your tax office will want. This tour walks through each feature, says whether your account has it switched on, and takes you to it. Two minutes, and you can leave and come back at any point.
tour.import_body: Drop a statement: every row is parsed and previewed before anything is written to your ledger. Revolut (CSV and PDF), Revolut crypto, Trading 212, DEGIRO, Interactive Brokers, ClickTrade / Saxo and a generic CSV are recognised. **Any crypto exchange's export** works too — Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, Bitpanda, Crypto.com, Koinly or whichever wrote it: just drop the file, the assistant works out its columns, and coin-to-coin swaps, staking rewards and deposits are valued at that day's price. Re-importing the same statement never duplicates a row. If your browser or work device blocks the file picker, **paste the statement text** instead — same parse, same preview, same commit. No statement to hand yet? **Load an example statement** puts a real one through the same parse, preview and commit, and **Clear last import** takes it back out again. Not ready to hand over a real statement? **Use demo transactions** on the Portfolio page fills the ledger with a made-up book of seven well-known stocks so every tab has something in it; it is labelled as demo wherever it shows, and your first real import deletes it. Shares moved between brokers are recognised even when the two statements name the company differently (an ISIN at one, the symbol at the other) or the arrival reads as a plain buy, and booking them as a move can be undone. Everything else in the app — positions, P/L, allocation, tax, dividends, fees — derives from this one ledger.
tour.positions_body: Your open lots with live prices, market value and weight in your reporting currency, plus which broker each holding actually sits in — a ticker split across two custodians shows as a split. Every ticker cell links through to its full page.
tour.risk_body: Two different questions, two sections. **Real return** is what your book actually did: time-weighted return (flow-adjusted, so a deposit never reads as a gain), money-weighted return (IRR), volatility and worst drawdown. **Risk of the current basket** is about what you hold today — allocation by sector, geography, currency and broker.
tour.projection_body: A range, not a prediction: 4,000 simulated scenarios from today's value, with **stocks and crypto moved separately** — each at its own real volatility and the correlation the two have shown. Stock growth is picked by **index reference** (MSCI World, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100) or, if you pick it, **your own holdings' rate** over the last two years — never by default; crypto starts at zero. Add a **monthly contribution** or a **target** and read the central case, the range and the chance of getting there, nominal or in today's money.
tour.tax_body: Sales matched against your lots — FIFO, LIFO, average cost or UK S104, whichever your country uses — realized gains per year net of commissions, and your jurisdiction's own rules on top. Twelve are implemented (ES, US, UK, DE, FR, IT, IE, PT, CA, AU, AE, CH), each with its own brackets, allowances, reporting flags and reporting currency. Set your tax residence in Profile: it decides which rules run and which currency the ledger is replayed in.
tour.income_body: Dividends per year and per position, with withholding and the credit you can claim — and, beside them, what your shares were **entitled** to: every company's dividend history priced by the shares your ledger held the day before each ex-date, so a payment your statement never carried still shows up, and next year's income is estimated on today's holdings. On Home, those payments no statement carried join **Recent transactions** too, summed into one row marked as an estimate that opens onto each payment. The **Fees** tab then separates what the broker charged from what the spread cost you: each execution is measured against the midpoint of its own session, so the markup that never appears on a statement becomes a number.
tour.review_body: Every holding scored on **business quality** and on **price**, then weighed against the rest of the book: what to sell, what to trim because it has grown too big or too risky, and what to add to. Each move comes sized in money, with the **tax** a sale adds this year and the date a buy stops undoing a loss sold inside the repurchase window. Below, your watchlist's names and any ticker you type are judged **buy, watch or pass** on the same scale. A screen over public fundamentals, not advice.
tour.pulse_body: Where the market is heading, read against your own book — ranked by how much of it you actually need. The top card answers it in five seconds: **risk appetite** as a 0-100 score on its own meter, with a ghost pin where the score stood a month ago, and beside it the same regime restated as what it does to your basket. **Why** opens the number up: all eight inputs — trend, breadth, volatility, term structure, credit, stocks-versus-bonds, junk demand and emerging markets — each with its own bar, a tick at where it stood a month ago and its raw level, so the score is auditable rather than a black box; an input that could not be built is named and greyed rather than quietly dropped. Alongside it, four readings that only exist as trends: how many indices and sectors are above their own trend, the stock/bond correlation (positive means both legs fall together), and which of the four rates regimes the last quarter describes. **Your book against this regime** measures your basket's sensitivity to equities, rates, credit and the dollar — each pill is the three-month drift, which is the regime moving under you without your having traded. **The detail** keeps the six long tables — indices, gauges, rates, inflation, rotation and cross-asset — behind one tab strip, every row the same shape: the level, the change over 1w / 1m / 3m / 12m, a sparkline, and whether the series is in an uptrend or turning. Every row there carries an **i** beside its name that says what the series is and how to read it, because “MOVE” and “2s10s” are not names that explain themselves.
tour.market_body: Price and chart, from one day to its whole listed history, with a zoom range that reports the move over exactly the window you selected and a measure between any two dates (two fingers on a phone, a right-click on a computer), plus financials, estimates, what **analysts** say (their rating, price targets and which way they are revising earnings), insider activity and news. The header names what the symbol is — stock, equity fund, bond fund, money market, closed-end fund, crypto or index — and the page shows the figures that kind is read by: a money-market fund shows its yield against the central bank's rate, not an RSI. Every KPI carries where it came from: **Fact** is verifiable in a filing, **Consensus** is analyst estimates, **Derived** is computed here. The search box at the top of the page works from anywhere in the app and labels each result with its kind. **Analyze with AI** in the header hands the whole company to the assistant — one click asks it about the business, the fundamentals, the valuation against its own history and how the position fits your book (funds and coins get their own question; an index, which nobody holds directly, gets none). A coin's page is read as a coin: how far under its **all-time high** it trades, where it sits in its **cycle** (Fear & Greed, the Mayer multiple, the 200-week average, the halving clock), what perpetual-swap traders pay to hold it (**funding** and **open interest**) and, when you hold it, its share of your crypto and what selling it at a loss would save in tax.
tour.sector_body: Pick a sector and see a comparable cohort of companies — the sector ETF's basket, widened with listed names outside the US — ranked on valuation and quality, with the best three called out and read for you. A second **best three** ranks the same cohort on technical momentum instead — trend, RSI, MACD, distance from its 52-week high, 3-month return and volume. Then see which of your holdings report next, beside the **tax deadlines** of your tax residence — flagged 30 days ahead — and the **ex-dividend dates** of what you hold, each with what it pays on your shares; last year's schedule fills the months nobody has declared yet. The same calendar marks the day a position sold at a loss can be **bought back** without deferring the loss, and the **Fed and ECB** rate decisions. Click any date and it says what it means for you — on a dividend, the cash that lands, net of the withholding your own statements show.
tour.assistant_body: The chat panel on the right, reachable from every page, with your real book in hand: it reads your positions, live quotes, filings and the web, and picks the analysis skill that fits the question. An empty thread opens with a few suggestions built from your own watchlist, so it has something useful to say before you have imported anything. It runs keyless on the shared TopStocks chain within a daily cap; connect your own provider key for no cap and any model that provider offers, or **sign in with OpenRouter** and have one minted on your account without copying anything. You can ask out loud as well: press the microphone on the composer and what you say is written into the field as you say it, then checked against the recording when you stop, so you read and fix it before it goes — the audio itself is never stored. While an answer is being written the send button becomes a stop button: press it and the answer stops where it is, keeping whatever it had already written. A connection that drops mid-answer is not read as a stop: the question is answered again the next time you open the app. Asked to change something — a favourite, an alert, a position — it shows what it understood and waits for **Confirm**, with **Edit** to fix a misheard price or symbol first. It can **fix your transactions** too — list, edit, delete or add rows, book a company two brokers spelled differently under one ticker, turn a sale and a buy into the **transfer** they were, or check the whole book for mistakes like these: each change is shown row by row with what it does to your holdings and realized gains before you confirm, and has an **Undo** after. On Telegram it waits for you to write "yes". A question that asks for a decision ("should I buy…?") is argued first by a **bull and a bear analyst**, and the answer weighs the two instead of taking the side the question leaned to. Ask for a chart — a share, a currency pair, an index, gold — and the app draws a **price chart** from real closes under the answer, with chips to switch the window, rather than the model sketching one from memory. Ask how you are doing against the S&P and **your own portfolio** is one of its lines, as its time-weighted return; ask how your book is split and it draws a **donut** by position, sector, country or currency, funds looked through. Asked which losses would offset this year's gains, it replays each through your tax rules and lists the **harvest candidates** with what each saves and the day a repurchase is clear; asked to take a position to a weight, it sizes the trade on a **target-weight slider** and prices the tax on the sale. It **remembers what you tell it about yourself** — say "remember that…", or mention a goal or a preference in passing — and each memory it saves, corrects or drops is shown under the answer with **Undo**; name something you discussed in an earlier conversation and that conversation is brought into the answer, with a link back to it. The list lives in **Settings → Memory** (and on your Profile), where you can edit it or switch it off.
tour.notify_body: A portfolio digest in the evening and price alerts during market hours, on Telegram. The digest ranks the day by what each holding did to your book in your reporting currency rather than by the loudest percentage, sets it against the S&P 500, and lists the week's ex-dividend dates and the payments already received — and, once, any tax deadline coming up in the next 30 days. Link your account once from the Notifications tab and the toggles start working; the jobs run server-side, so nothing depends on you having the app open.
tour.investor_body: Risk tolerance, horizon, focus and constraints. The assistant reads it before answering, so the analysis is framed for your mandate instead of a generic one. The **focus** areas do one more thing: the watchlist tab then offers example tickers from them that you do not already follow — examples to look at, never recommendations, and adding them removes nothing you have.
tour.prefs_body: Reporting currency, language, tax residence and the bracket inputs your jurisdiction reads, grouped into three cards; the tax card states what the choice decides (cost currency, share matching, tax year) instead of describing it. Nothing here has a Save button — every change is written as you make it. It is also where the ledger exports to CSV, where an account deletes itself, and where this tour lives whenever you want it again. The **Claude** card holds the connector address that lets Claude read your book, and lists every app connected to it with a **Revoke** beside each.
tour.daily_body: One AI card on Home, generated once a day (it turns over at 09:00 in your own timezone): a headline naming the day's few things, then three parts by default. **Portfolio** sets your book's move today, this week and this month beside the S&P 500's, with the month drawn. **Today's alerts** are your own alerts the price crossed in the latest session — one that fired days ago is not on the card. **Worth a look** has a line for each thing that came up: a print on a name you hold or watch in the next two weeks and how the latest ones did against the estimate, a **Fed or ECB** decision around the corner, the **tax calendar** (a filing deadline, the year closing with gains or losses still open, the next savings bracket, the day a sold loss can be bought back), positions at a 52-week edge and **the market your book sits in**. The **pencil** in the card's corner changes that: write what it should tell you each day, a line per thing, and each line becomes a section of its own, in your order, under your fired alerts — your biggest moves, the **events of the next seven days** (results, ex-dividend dates, the Fed and the ECB, tax deadlines), **insider trades** at your largest holdings (SEC Form 4, BaFin for German issuers), the last days' **headlines** naming your companies, the **8-Ks** they filed this week, which **big investors** added to or cut them last quarter (13F, dated), a review of your **exit criteria** against your alerts and notes, the main indices, rates or crypto, a long-term proposal marked as one. Start from a template or your own words; it reads back what it will fetch before the first card, and a line it has no data for says so rather than call the day quiet. The chat keeps the same list when you ask it for something every day. It **remembers what it told you**: a trigger it already showed stays off until its figure moves or its date gets closer. Each line opens its own **analysis**: the comparison it invites, made — the company against its peers, its sector and the S&P 500, its business figures and the analysts' consensus, what a sale saves in tax, which positions explain a month behind the index — as a verdict, a few points and the tables behind them, and every figure in the prose is checked against what was fetched. If no model answers it falls back to the same facts and tables without the prose. Home's cards are yours to order: **Customise** moves, hides and adds them, and the order follows your account to every device.
tour.news_2026_09_tax_body: ES, US, UK, DE, FR, IT, IE, PT, CA and AU, each with its own lot matching, brackets and reporting flags — pick your residence in Profile. Positions also record which broker holds them now.
tour.news_2026_09_daily_body: One AI briefing a day on the dashboard, on the numbers Home already has — no prompt to write.
tour.news_2026_09_fees_body: Commissions and estimated spread per broker — the execution cost your statement never itemises.
tour.news_2026_09_demo_body: The Portfolio page can now fill itself with a made-up book of seven well-known stocks, so you can see positions, risk, dividends, fees and the tax report working before importing anything — your first real import removes it.
tour.news_2026_09_pulse_body: A new page built around direction rather than level, and ranked for a five-second read: a 0-100 risk-appetite score with its eight inputs laid open beside it, your own basket's sensitivities and how far they have drifted, and six tables — indices, gauges, rates, inflation, rotation and cross-asset — behind one tab strip, every row carrying its 1w/1m/3m/12m change, a sparkline and a trend label.
tour.news_2026_09_profile_body: Every setting is a row with its own explanation, grouped into Interface, Tax residence and Data — the tax card now states the rules your jurisdiction actually applies, and the whole ledger exports as CSV.
tour.news_2026_09_weekly_body: A new message, once a week, for the question five daily digests never answer: how is this going. Week, month and **year-to-date** in money and percent with the index beside each, the names that actually moved the book, the cash that landed, the week ahead — and how **concentrated** you have become, with the drift since last Sunday. Switch it off in Profile → Notifications.
tour.watchlist_body: The list every other page reads: Overview, Screener, Earnings and the ticker picker all run on it. Add a name by **searching** it — your own list, coins, funds, the SEC company map and every venue Yahoo quotes, so a symbol arrives with its real name instead of being spelled from memory. **Groups** are the app's grouping primitive: a ticker can sit in several, the list can be grouped by them, and Overview renders a section per group. Everything you edit here writes immediately.
tour.news_2026_09_watchlist_body: Adding a ticker is a **search** across your list, coins, funds, the SEC map and worldwide listings — no more typing a symbol into a blank grid row. **Groups** are a picker rather than a comma string, the list can be **grouped by** them, and a group can be renamed or dissolved from its own header. Every edit saves as you make it, and phones get one control row per holding instead of a grid that pans sideways.
tour.news_2026_09_1_voice_body: The composer now carries a **microphone**, inside the field at its bottom-right corner: record the question and it lands in the field as text, transcribed on the same keyless chain the answers come from, for you to check and correct before sending it. Only the transcript is kept — the recording is dropped as soon as it has been read — and the turn is badged as spoken, so a misheard ticker explains itself on reload. It is worth most on a phone, where typing out a five-line question is the worst part of asking it.
tour.news_2026_09_2_splitfix_body: A share bought before a **20:1** split and never sold used to keep the share count and the price the trade ticket carried, so the position read as a deep loss against a post-split market price. **Check for missing splits** on the Import page now compares each holding's buy price against the market close of that day: when the price is still on the old scale it names the split, shows what the share count becomes, and adds the row on your say-so. The money you paid never changes — only the shares behind it, and the average buy price that follows. The price chart follows: your buy and sell markers now sit on the candles' own scale, so an old lot plots where it really was and its return to today is the real one.
tour.news_2026_09_2_transfers_title: Shares that changed broker, not owner
tour.news_2026_09_2_transfers_body: Move a holding to another broker and the statements disagree about what happened: the old broker prints the departure as a **sale at the day's market price**, the new one just lists the shares as a balance. Your book then reported a capital gain nobody made, restarted the holding period, and taxed the whole thing. Transfers are now their own kind of ledger row — no gain is realized, the original purchase date and cost basis carry across, and only the broker holding the shares changes. DEGIRO exports are read directly (a departure carries no order id, no venue and no commission, because nobody traded), and for a book already imported the wrong way the Import page offers to repair it: it pairs a sale with the arrival that carries the **same cost basis**, which is the one thing a real sale-and-repurchase could not produce.
tour.news_2026_09_2_sectors_title: Sector screen, in place of the watchlist screener
tour.news_2026_09_2_sectors_body: Pick one of eleven sectors and compare a cohort you did not have to assemble: the sector ETF's basket, widened with listed companies outside the US. The **best three** are called out by the same percentile score the comps table uses — across this cohort's valuation and quality, which means it says "the best three of these", not "the best three anywhere". The old watchlist screener is gone; its filters and columns live here.
tour.news_2026_09_4_sector_tech_title: A second best three, on technical momentum
tour.news_2026_09_4_sector_tech_body: The sector screen now ranks its cohort a second way: **trend** (the 50 vs. 200-day average), **RSI**, **MACD**, distance from the 52-week high, 3-month return and volume — a separate podium from the valuation-and-quality one, so the two never blend into a single score.
tour.news_2026_09_4_projection_title: Where your portfolio could be in five years
tour.news_2026_09_4_projection_body: A new **Projection** tab in Portfolio draws the fan of values your book could reach in 1, 3, 5 or 10 years, with stocks and crypto modelled separately, index references for growth and the **chance of reaching your target**.
tour.news_2026_09_3_newapp_body: Every screen — dashboard, portfolio, pulse, sectors, earnings, import, the ticker page and the assistant — has been rebuilt as a single front end, reading the same data through one API. Same links, same numbers: it loads once and moves between pages without reloading.
tour.news_2026_09_5_daily_more_title: The daily action, analysed line by line
tour.news_2026_09_5_daily_more_body: Each line of Home's daily card opens its own **analysis**: rather than suggesting a comparison, it makes it — the company against its peers, its sector and the S&P 500, what a sale saves in tax, which positions explain a month behind the index — with the tables beside it. The card also **remembers what it told you**, so it changes every day instead of repeating itself.
tour.news_2026_09_6_import_title: Import, rebuilt around its four steps
tour.news_2026_09_6_import_body: Platform, statement, review, confirm — in that order, with **Confirm** pinned over the rows so it never scrolls away, and a chip per group that jumps straight to the rejected or warned ones. Beside it sit **your portfolio now**, the **repairs** waiting (shares that only changed broker, missing splits) and the **last import** with its undo; on a phone they fold away and Confirm stays at the foot of the screen.
tour.news_2026_09_7_whatif_title: What if you sold? Ask the assistant
tour.news_2026_09_7_whatif_body: Ask **what you would pay if you sold** a holding — "what if I sell half my NVDA?" — and the sale runs through the same tax engine as the Tax tab: your residence's lot order, this year's other gains, the brackets. Under the answer sits a **slider** over the shares you hold; move it and the proceeds, the realised gain and this year's extra tax follow, with no AI in the loop. Nothing is sold.
tour.news_2026_10_memory_body: Tell the assistant your goals, your horizon or what you avoid — "remember that…", or just in passing — and it **keeps it for every later conversation** — the daily action and the Telegram messages read the same memory, so they head the same way. Each memory it saves, corrects or drops shows under the answer with **Undo**, and naming something from an earlier conversation brings that conversation into the answer. See and edit the list in **Settings → Memory**.
tour.news_2026_10_routines_title: The daily card answers what you ask every day
tour.news_2026_10_routines_body: Ask the assistant for something **every day** — "each morning show me how NVDA is doing" — or ask it the same thing on three different days, and Home's daily card answers it before you type, every figure checked against the data fetched.
tour.news_2026_10_claude_body: Add TopStocks to **claude.ai, Claude Desktop or Claude Code** as a connector and ask about your book with your real figures: positions, returns, income, risk, tax — and it reads **the same profile and memory** as the assistant here, so it starts from your goals and limits. Claude asks you to sign in here and approve it, and it only reads unless you tick the box that **lets it make changes** — then it can fix your transactions too, showing each change before it applies it, and every change can be undone. Nothing is ever bought or sold. In claude.ai and Desktop the overview and the performance are **drawn in the chat**, with a link back to the page; the address and the apps you connected live in Profile, where one press revokes any of them.
tour.news_2026_10_1_fixbook_title: Fix your book from the chat
tour.news_2026_10_1_fixbook_body: A transfer imported as a sale and a buy, one company under two tickers, a trade imported twice: tell the assistant — "my Grifols shows twice" — and it finds the rows, shows **what the fix does to your holdings and gains**, and applies it only when you confirm. Edit, delete or add rows the same way; every change has an **Undo**.
tour.news_2026_10_2_home_body: Press **Customise** on Home to drag its cards into the order you read them, put away the ones you skip and add others: **Portfolio risk**, **Dividends**, **Tax year** and **Sector rotation**, each a short cut of its own screen. Home now opens on **Market** — the Pulse's mood score and the main indices, the VIX, the US 10-year, the euro, gold, oil and bitcoin, moved over today, the week or the month.
tour.news_2026_10_2_brief_title: Write what the daily card tells you
tour.news_2026_10_2_brief_body: Press the **pencil** on Home's daily card and write what it should tell you each day, a line per thing — your biggest moves, next week's events, what insiders bought or sold, a review of your exit criteria, a long-term proposal. Each line becomes **a section of the card**, in your order, under your fired alerts, and before the first card it reads back **what it will fetch**. Delete it and the default card comes back.
tour.news_2026_10_3_crypto_title: A coin read as a coin
tour.news_2026_10_3_crypto_body: Open a coin and its page no longer reads like a share's: its distance from the **all-time high** sits beside the price, halvings and ETF approvals are marked on the chart, and a **Cycle** card sets the market's Fear & Greed and bitcoin dominance next to the coin's Mayer multiple, 200-week average and the halving clock. **Derivatives** shows what leveraged traders pay to hold it, and, only when you hold it, a card on **your holding** gives its share of your crypto and of your book and, at a loss, what selling it would save in tax.
tour.news_2026_10_4_analysts_title: What analysts say about a share
tour.news_2026_10_4_analysts_body: A share's page has an **Analysts** section: the consensus rating and how it has moved month by month, the 12-month **price targets** — median beside mean, since one outlier drags a mean — with how far apart they are, and the **EPS revisions** of the last 7, 30 and 90 days. It is consensus, not fact, and with fewer than three analysts it says so instead of drawing a split.
tour.news_2026_10_5_review_title: What to sell and what to add to
tour.news_2026_10_5_review_body: A new **Sell or add** page ranks your holdings sell, trim, hold or add on business quality and price, each move sized in money with the **tax** it costs, and plots them on a quality-against-price map. Type any ticker to weigh it beside your watchlist as **buy, watch or pass** — nothing is followed until you choose to.
